title: Ordered Unique Intersection
description: Return the unique values that appear in both input lists, in the order of their first appearance in `left`. Values are strings.

solution.explanation: Build a set from the right side for fast membership checks, then scan the left side. A second set prevents repeated results while the list preserves the left side’s order. The second set also avoids adding the same match twice.

wrongSolutions:
def ordered_intersection(left, right):
    return sorted(set(left) & set(right))

def ordered_intersection(left,right):
    return [x for x in left if x in right]

tests.hint: No left-side values means no output.
Follow left order rather than right order.
Repeated left values appear only once.
Disjoint lists have an empty intersection.
Membership does not reorder the left list.
Skip values absent on the right.
This larger case checks membership and order.
The right-side order is intentionally different.
An empty right side has no matches.
